title: Mission Control telemetry sprint brief
content:
Purpose: quick, actionable sprint briefing for a small cross-functional team to land a low-cost, high-utility telemetry surface for token-serving flows. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — combine definitions, lightweight tracing conventions, dashboard wireframes and a sampling/cost guardrail plan so the sprint can ship with predictable ingest cost.

Context and goals:
- Primary customer: production inference services (hosted + dedicated) serving streaming token workloads. Need observability that supports: P95/P99 regression detection, root-cause for latency spikes, and quick correlation of model variant fallbacks to user-facing error rates.
- Sprint outcome (MVP): a single Mission Control dashboard per service class + an alerting matrix + a tracing sampling policy that targets 1.5–2.5x baseline trace volume under load.

Top-level metrics (definition + query sketch + why):
1) user_request_latency_ms - histogram of end-to-end request duration (ingress timestamp -> last-token-sent)
   - suggested aggregation: p50, p95, p99, and median-tail (p99.9 for high-traffic routes)
   - query sketch: histogram_percentile(duration_ms_bucket, [50,95,99]) grouped by route, model_version, region
   - why: primary SLO lens; needs to be correlated with token_count and kv_cache_hit to avoid false positives.

2) per_token_emission_latency_ms - average time between token generation events inside the runtime (kernel exec start -> token emitted)
   - important for isolating runtime hot paths vs network/ingress overhead

3) kv_cache_hit_ratio - ratio of requests that used a prefix/KV cache hit (boolean label on request)
   - formula: sum(kv_cache_hit == 1) / sum(requests) by model_variant

4) batch_size_distribution - distribution of tokens per batch and requests per batch
   - why: determines cost/latency tradeoff; use percentiles and mode per timeslice

5) fallback_rate - percent of requests that hit a fallback model/region/queue
   - track with labels: fallback_type (model_variant, region, capacity_tier) and reason tag where available

6) inference_error_rate - classified by code (model_error, runtime_oom, timeout, malformed_request)
   - alert threshold guidance: P0 if sustained >0.5% at service level for 5m; P1 if >0.2% and rising

Tracing conventions (lightweight, structured):
- Trace root: request.rid (request-id) -> attach initial context: route, customer_tier, model_version, origin_region.
- Span naming: <component>.<operation> e.g., ingress.http.receive, runtime.kv_lookup, runtime.kernel.dispatch, output.stream.flush
- Minimal tags (must exist on all traces): request.rid, model.version, seq_len, token_count, batch_id (if batched), kv_cache_hit(boolean), route
- Error tagging: span.error_type (one of: timeout, oom, model_fail, infra_fail, client_input)
- Latency anchors: record timestamps at ingress.receive, runtime.start, runtime.kv_return, kernel.exec_start, kernel.exec_end, emit.token_start, emit.token_end. Use those anchors to compute per-token and per-request breakdowns.
- Sampling decision points (see below) should be recorded as trace tags: sampling.policy and sampling.reasons list.

Sampling policy (goal: informative traces while bounding storage cost):
- Baseline: 5% uniform sampling across all requests for full spans.
- Elevated sampling triggers (force full traces):
  * any request that triggers fallback_rate path (fallback_type != null) -> 100% sample for 30m county window per route
  * errors (inference_error_rate event) -> 100% sample for that request and 50% of similar requests for 1h
  * latency outliers: if request latency > p99 for last 10m for that route, sample at 50% for next 10m
- Adaptive headroom: when CPU/GPU trace ingestion budget > 90% spent, automatically downsample non-error traces to 1% and prioritize fallback/error traces. Implementation note: expose a budget metric and a boolean tag sample_budget_low=true so processors can drop low-priority traces.

Dashboard wireframe notes (Mission Control):
- Top row: SLO health (p95 latency vs target) + traffic QPS + error rate heatmap (by route/model)
- Middle row: breakdown panel (latency waterfall: ingress -> runtime-> kernel -> network), batch size distribution histogram, kv_cache_hit ratio trend
- Bottom row: anomalies & recent full traces (feed) + rollback indicator (if rollout system signals degraded model_version in last 12h)
- Drilldowns: clicking a latency waterfall links to trace query pre-filtered by model_version and time window. Include quick filters for customer_tier and region.

Alerting matrix (initial recommendations):
- Latency SLO burn: if p95 > target for 10m AND traffic > 20% baseline => P1
- Error spike: if inference_error_rate increases by 3x over baseline in 5m and >0.1% absolute => P0
- Trace ingest budget: if trace_bytes_per_minute > budget * 0.95 => ops paging + auto-downsample
- Fallback spike: if fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 5m AND correlated with increased latency => P1

Operational playbook snippets (runbook links in artifacts):
- When P0 error spike: run fast check list -> identify model_version, recent rollouts, infra events (node restarts) -> attach 3 full traces and a heatmap snapshot to incident ticket.
- When unexpected latency: check kv_cache_hit_ratio first; if dropped by >15% correlate with recent model changes or cache invalidation events.

Data cost guardrails and KPI targets for this sprint:
- Target trace volume: < 2.5x current baseline in steady-state (measured by trace_bytes_per_minute)
- Target metrics cardinality: limit high-cardinality tags to three stable dims for dashboards (route, model_version, region). Use hashed id for customer when needed but avoid as primary grouping.
- Budget enforcement: annotate expensive traces via trace_cost_estimate tag and reject non-critical high-cost traces when budget_low flag is set.

Open questions / TODOs (action items for sprint):
- TODO: finalize exact p99 percentile buckets for per_token_emission_latency (should we use 99.5 vs 99.9?). Owner: Liam.
- TODO: implement sample_budget_low metric and a cheap aggregator in front of trace collectors. Owner: Priya.
- TODO: dashboard wireframe mockups and a small user test with SREs and a customer success rep. Owner: Diego.

Notes to self / meeting crumbs:
- Slack thread: #obs-mission-control had discussion re: trace cost model on 2026-01-28 (see linked_artifacts).
- Keep interface simple for first pass, focus on signal-to-noise ratio rather than exhaustive coverage.

Appendix (quick queries and alert pseudo-rules):
- p95 latency query sketch: histogram_percentile(duration_ms_bucket, 95) by route, model_version
- fallback_rate query sketch: sum(fallback_type != "") / sum(requests) by route
- sample budget rule: if rate(trace_bytes_min) / rate(budget_bytes_min) > 0.95 => set sample_budget_low=true

This doc is intentionally lightweight and action-oriented. If we land the sampling policy and the Mission Control dashboard MVP, we should expect to reduce mean investigation time for latency/regression incidents by ~40% while keeping telemetry costs within a predictable cap.

If you iterate on this, please update linked_artifacts and mark status when ready for launch.
